examples.title: See The Difference
examples.subtitle: Transform vague requests into precise, results-driven prompts

example1.before: Write a blog post about productivity
example1.after: As an experienced content strategist, write a 1,200-word blog post about productivity hacks for remote workers. Target audience: tech professionals aged 25-40. Tone: Professional yet approachable. Include 5 actionable tips with real examples.

example2.after: As a senior marketing consultant, create a 3-email welcome sequence for new subscribers to a meditation app. Audience: stressed professionals seeking work-life balance. Tone: Calm and empathetic. Each email should be 150-200 words with a clear CTA.

example3.after: As a social media expert, create 5 Instagram captions for a sustainable fashion brand launching eco-friendly sneakers. Target: environmentally conscious millennials. Tone: Inspiring and authentic. Include relevant hashtags and emojis.

example4.after: As a patient educator, explain quantum computing to a 12-year-old with no technical background. Use simple analogies from everyday life. Keep it under 300 words. Make it engaging and avoid jargon completely.

example5.after: As a B2B sales expert, write a cold outreach email to CTOs of mid-sized tech companies introducing our cybersecurity solution. Tone: Professional and value-focused. Length: 150 words max. Include a clear meeting request CTA.

step1.title: What are you trying to achieve?
step1.subtitle: Be specific about your goal. The clearer you are, the better the result.
step1.placeholder: e.g., Write a blog post about sustainable living
step1.learnMoreDesc: This is your main goal or objective. Think of it as the 'what' you want the AI to create or help you with. Be clear and specific — vague requests lead to vague results.
examples: Write a product description for eco-friendly water bottles
Create a marketing email for a new app launch
Generate ideas for social media posts about productivity

step2.title: Who's your audience?
step2.subtitle: This helps the AI understand who you're writing for and tailor the response.
step2.placeholder: e.g., Tech-savvy millennials interested in sustainability
step2.learnMoreDesc: Context provides background information that shapes the AI's understanding. This includes your audience, situation, constraints, or any relevant details. The more context you provide, the more tailored and useful the response will be.
examples: Small business owners looking to grow their online presence
Students learning programming for the first time
Busy parents seeking meal planning tips

step3.title: Which AI are you using?
step3.subtitle: Different AIs have different strengths. This helps tailor your prompt.
step3.learnMoreDesc: Different AI models have unique strengths and formatting preferences. ChatGPT excels at creative and conversational tasks. Claude is great for detailed analysis. Gemini handles multimodal tasks well.

step4.title: What tone should the output have?
step4.subtitle: Tone shapes how your AI responds. Choose what fits your audience. (Optional - you can skip this)
step4.learnMoreDesc: Tone determines the personality and style of the AI's response. It affects word choice, sentence structure, and overall feel. Match the tone to your audience and purpose for maximum impact.

step5.title: Any special rules or requirements?
step5.subtitle: Special instructions help shape precision. Add formatting needs or content limits.
step5.placeholder: e.g., Keep it under 500 words, use bullet points, include 3 examples
step5.learnMoreTitle: When do I need special rules?
step5.learnMoreDesc: Requirements and constraints define the boundaries and format of the output. This includes word limits, structural preferences (bullet points, headings), must-have elements, or things to avoid.
examples: Keep under 500 words, use bullet points

step6.title: What role should the AI play?
step6.subtitle: This tells the AI how to act and what perspective to use.
step6.placeholder: e.g., Expert marketer, helpful teacher, creative writer
step6.learnMoreDesc: Assigning a role gives the AI a persona and expertise level to embody. This shapes its perspective, knowledge base, and approach.
examples: Senior marketing consultant with 10 years experience
Patient educator who explains complex topics simply
Creative copywriter specializing in emotional storytelling
